paper_title: Oil-Price Exposure as a Single-Factor Smart-Beta Strategy
selected_experiment: Sections 5-7 methodology (no empirical table): OILP regime portfolios - constrained long-short optimized positive (+0.25), neutral (0.00) and negative (-0.10) OILP-exposure equity portfolios, with a timing signal s(t) selecting which regime to hold at each rebalance date

economic_rationale.value: Oil-price innovations affect firms differently through production costs, revenues, demand conditions and discount-rate channels; conditionally, higher oil returns favor positive oil exposure and lower oil returns favor negative exposure. No unconditional premium is claimed.

evidence.quote: Oil-price innovations can affect firms differently through production costs, revenues, demand conditions, and discount-rate channels.

universe_and_filters.value: the available equity universe on each construction date; no universe definition or filters stated

evidence.quote: On each chosen construction date, solve a constrained optimization across the available equity universe.

value: monthly oil price level series P(t) (OilPrices.csv) to compute oil changes
risk control series X(t) (e.g., market, credit, consumer, and employment proxies)
historical residual returns from a trailing cross-sectional regression (optimizer objective)

evidence.quote: The attached CSV alone is insufficient to estimate OILP; separate equity returns and control series are required.

signal_formula_words.value: OILP is each security's slope coefficient b_i,oil from a time-series regression of its returns on monthly simple oil-price changes plus other risk controls, estimated on a training sample. A constrained long-short optimizer builds positive, neutral and negative OILP-target portfolios (maximizing exposure to historical residual returns subject to the OILP target, other factor targets, gross long/short allocations and name bounds); a timing signal s(t) picks positive if s(t) >= h, negative if s(t) <= -h, neutral otherwise.

evidence.quote: The coefficient b_i,oil is the security-level OILP exposure.

signal_formula_symbols.value: r_i(t) = a_i + b_i,oil r_oil(t) + G_i X(t) + e_i(t); r_oil(t) = P(t) / P(t-1) - 1; B_oil(w) = sum_i w_i b_i,oil; max_w sum_i w_i e_i subject to target OILP exposure
